Prevention: Citrus greening is a serious disease of citrus caused by a bacterium and transmitted by citrus psyllid
Source certified healthy seedlings from a certified nursery
Leave flower strips along the edges of the farm/ intercrop with beans, black night shade or similar flowering plants to encourage natural enemies (parasitic wasp) that feed on psyllid nymphs
Monitoring: Check for leaves that look yellowed or mottled with green midribs on the trees in neighbouring farms to confirm if disease is in the area.
It is important for neighbouring farmers to take collective action to control the disease vectors, if the disease is present.

Yellowing process of leaves due to citrus greening disease does not follow any defined pattern while the nutrient deficiency yellowing is symmetric between left and right leaf side next to the green midrib
Look for brown psyllid insects with a light brown head, with a head down and tail up posture as it feeds (citrus psyllids).
They jump and fly off when branches are shaken
Look for the psyllids on new leaf growth as they like feeding on young leaves
Look for the psyllids early in the morning as they are inactive during this time
Consider action when the disease is in your area, and be quick if it is in neighbouring fields
Control for the disease is too late once it has been introduced into the orchard
Citrus greening can be confused with other diseases such as citrus stubborn and tristeza which also cause yellowing of the leaves.
Uneven ripening (greening) and uneven shaped fruits are diagnostic.
Diseased trees also show poor growth and dieback.
Direct Control: Remove and destroy young infested trees by burning at a safe place outside the orchard.
Uproot and replace diseased seedlings and young trees as they will never bear fruits.
Destroy the diseased uprooted trees by drying in sun or burning.
This is needed to prevent further disease spread.
Use biopesticides such as neem oil to control the citrus psyllids that transmit the disease.
Neem oil kills psyllids by suffocation and is a repellent for psyllids
Restrictions: When using a pesticide or botanical, always wear protective clothing and follow the instructions on the product label
